images.alt: Paulus schrijft de slotgroet — 2 Tessalonicensen 3:17; tekstillustratie.
images.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Photorealistic illustration of an explicit biblical comparison or event, first-century Roman Judea and Galilee, landscape 3:2, natural materials and daylight, anatomically coherent people with exactly two arms and animals with correct limbs; fully covering modest opaque robes. No modern objects, readable writing, portrait of God the Father, blood, injury or watermark. 2 Thessalonians 3:17 says Paul writes the greeting with his own hand as the sign in every letter. Close medium shot of a mature bearded Paul in an ordinary modest first-century room, seated at a small wooden table, carefully adding the final greeting to a sheet of papyrus with a reed pen. One right hand holds the pen naturally, the other hand rests on the far edge of the sheet, precisely two arms. Warm window light, concentration, no readable writing, no modern binding or fountain pen. This is the specific handwritten closing sign, not another anonymous group discussion.
